title: Raleigh police use Marinus Analytics' Traffic Jam to link phone numbers and photos across cities in a live trafficking case
summary: Raleigh police detectives used Traffic Jam, a Marinus Analytics tool that searches escort ads by phone number and face, to corroborate victims' accounts of a trafficker's movements.
account: The case described was ongoing. Major Richard Hoffman of the Raleigh Police Department described Traffic Jam to CBN. It lets investigators link a potential victim to another victim and then to a suspect. Its image search returns historical images tied to the same phone number or similar image. Detective Rob Pereira described pulling a phone number from a Colorado police report into Traffic Jam to see where and when it had been used. This corroborated several victims' accounts of where the trafficker was taking them. Marinus co-founder Cara Jones described the tool as applying artificial intelligence to publicly available ad data. CBN states that Traffic Jam has helped recover hundreds of victims. Futurism (2018) repeats a similar claim from chief executive Emily Kennedy with an 88 percent success rate. No individually attributable rescue is documented.
purpose: Mine online sex advertisements (text, phone numbers, facial recognition on images) to help law enforcement find trafficking victims and link cases.
developer: Marinus Analytics (origin: Carnegie Mellon University undergraduate project)
